rows.question: How many days after an expense is incurred must it be submitted for reimbursement?
rows.answer: Expenses must be submitted within 30 business days of the date the expense was incurred [1][4].

rows.question: How many days per week can employees work remotely?
rows.answer: Employees may work remotely one day per week. Remote Work Requests cannot be approved for more than one day per week [2].

rows.question: Who gives final approval for a remote work agreement?
rows.answer: The Divisional Vice President/Division Head gives final approval for a Remote Work Agreement [1][3].

rows.question: How much notice should departments give before terminating a remote work agreement?
rows.answer: Departments should give 14 calendar days’ notice before terminating a Remote Work Agreement, unless extenuating circumstances make such notice impracticable [1].

rows.question: How many weeks of FMLA leave are eligible staff entitled to?
rows.answer: Eligible staff are entitled to up to 12 weeks of FMLA leave [5][1].

rows.question: How long must an employee have worked to be eligible for FMLA?
rows.answer: To be eligible for FMLA, a staff member must have been employed for at least 12 months and have worked at least 1,250 hours during the 12 months immediately preceding the start of the leave [3].

rows.question: When should an employee report a work-related injury?
rows.answer: They should report it immediately — notify your supervisor right away. If you cannot return to work, also immediately notify the leaves administration manager in the Office of Human Resources. (Claims must be filed within five calendar days of the injury.) [1][2]

rows.question: What tuition benefits are available?
rows.answer:
Summary of tuition benefits (from the staff handbook):

- Full‑time eligible staff:
  - 100% tuition remission for up to two courses at a time taken at Carnegie Mellon [1].
  - University pays 50% of tuition for courses taken at other institutions (must be credit‑bearing and career‑related) [1].

- Part‑time eligible staff:
  - University pays tuition for one course at a time taken at Carnegie Mellon.
  - No tuition payment for courses at other institutions for part‑time employees [1].

- Dependent children of eligible staff:
  - Tuition benefits for dependent children enrolled in undergraduate programs at Carnegie Mellon or other accredited institutions (includes bachelor/associate degree programs, trade school, certification programs, or community college before age 30) [1][3].
  - Staff must have completed three full years of service and be full‑time benefits‑eligible (three‑year requirement may be reduced/waived for prior qualifying service) [1].
  - Children must meet IRS dependency criteria and be the staff member’s biological, adopted, or stepchild, or the child of the employee’s domestic partner [1].

- Other notes:
  - Tuition benefits are subject to applicable federal income and Social Security tax and will be withheld from pay [3].
  - Staff must apply through Workday for employee tuition benefits [3].

rows.question: How much paid sick leave is provided?
rows.answer: Part‑time staff not eligible for PTO receive 40 hours of paid sick leave per calendar year (48 hours if they work in the city of Los Angeles). Up to 40 hours of unused sick leave may be carried over year‑to‑year, with an accrual cap of 80 hours. Paid sick leave may be used in hourly increments [3][1].

rows.question: How many weeks of paid parental leave are available to all parents?
rows.answer: All parents are eligible for up to six weeks of paid parental leave [2][1].

rows.question: What is the maximum military caregiver leave?
rows.answer: The maximum Military Caregiver Leave is up to 26 workweeks of leave in a single 12‑month period [1][2].

rows.question: What should be prepared before a new employee's first day?
rows.answer:
Prepare the following before the new employee’s first day:

- Maintain communication and send a welcome/confirmation (notify of any hiring delays; confirm work schedule, salary, and start/report date; arrange 1st‑day orientation meeting) [2].
- Assign an onboarding sponsor (or manager/supervisor) and confirm who will onboard the employee [2][1].
- Prepare a Welcome Packet and other resources to help transition into the job [2].
- Submit requests for new‑employee logistics: badge/ID/building access, parking/commuting info, workstation (computer, email, network, system and training accounts), telephone and distribution list additions, standard office equipment and supplies, any reasonable accommodations, and any other department‑specific items [1].
- Prepare department/unit staff for the employee’s arrival (provide background, role/responsibilities; send an email introduction and schedule meetings for the employee’s first week) [1].
- Register the employee for new employee orientation and any mandatory or job‑related training; develop the overall onboarding plan with action items, dates, and a training schedule [1].
